newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks likely to trend lower.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks likely to trend lower.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are likely to trend lower on Thursday, with investors cautiously waiting for the next move from Wall Street as well as U.S. economic data, brokers said.
"The market should be a bit cautious because it is difficult to predict what Wall Street will do tonight," said Peter Lui in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index closed Tuesday's half-day session down 29.30 points at 13,451.45 in active trade.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index ended its last session of 1996 down 2.87 points at 13,448.58 in very slow trading.
The Dow declined on Tuesday but volume was very low, leaving brokers uncertain about what an active market will do, said Lui.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 101.10 points or 1.54 percent to 6,448.27 on Tuesday after U.S. economic data showed a greater-than-expected 14.2 percent rise in the sale of single family homes and a four-point jump in the consumer confidence index in November.
The U.S. long bond also slumped on the news, with the price falling 1-9/32 to yield 6.64 percent compared with 6.59 percent at the close of Monday trading.
Analysts noted that during 1996 U.S. stocks moved closely in line with bonds and that the Hang Seng Index has shown a close correlation to U.S. bond market movements.
The U.S. jobless claims report for the week ending December 28 is due out on Thursday, along with the National Association of Purchasing Managers' report for December.
